strings.app.name: Refund Desk
strings.banner.fixture: SIMULATION: PayPal answers on this screen come from synthetic fixtures. No real PayPal sandbox, no real money.

strings.home.tagline: A buyer writes about a problem order. A reader proposes a refund. Your rules decide what goes out by itself. Even when the reader is compromised, automatic refunds remain within merchant-set limits. Larger requests, and requests that match a recognized suspicious pattern, wait for the owner; some patterns are refused outright.

strings.arena.title: Injection Arena
strings.arena.intro: Write a hostile message as a buyer. A reader proposes a refund. The same authority that runs the Refund Desk decides, and it reads your raw words itself instead of trusting the reader. Only the payment provider differs: here it is a fake.
strings.arena.text_hint: Try a prompt injection, a duplicate claim, a changed amount, an urgent or authoritative tone, a claim that the policy changed, or a request to ignore the rules.
strings.arena.library_hint: Click one to load it into the box, then send it.
strings.arena.result_empty: Send a message or load a preset. The reader's proposal, the gate's decision and the receipt appear here.
strings.arena.reader_ASK: No clear amount, so it would ask the buyer. It proposed no refund.
strings.arena.reader_NONE: It read no refund request. It proposed nothing.
strings.arena.fooled_badge: The reader went along with this message.
strings.arena.gloss.ALLOW: Inside the owner's policy. In this simulation the amount is released.
strings.arena.gloss.ESCALATE: Held for the owner. Nothing moved.
strings.arena.flags_title: Attack signals found by the gate's own scan
strings.arena.flags_none: No attack signal found in the message.
strings.arena.flag_changed: These signals changed the decision. Without them the gate would have said {decision} under {rule}.
strings.arena.flag_same: Without the signals the decision would be the same.
strings.arena.flag.CONTRADICTORY_INTENT: Request taken back or made conditional
strings.arena.flag.obfuscated: hidden by spacing or look-alike letters
strings.arena.diff_title: What the reader proposed versus what the gate allowed
strings.arena.receipt_sig_bad: This record's signature does not check out.
strings.arena.court_link: Read this case as a court transcript
strings.arena.budget_line: Automatic refunds add up to at most {cap} per order and {daily} per day.
strings.arena.policy_summary: Automatic refunds on one order add up to {cap}. One refund you approve can be up to {ceiling}. Daily budget for automatic refunds {daily}. Evidence required: {evidence}.
strings.arena.policy_edit: Change it in the Policy Builder
strings.arena.copy_hint: Messages sent here are stored in this arena's receipt chain on this machine.
strings.arena.rule.G1: The message tries to give the reader new orders or to switch the rules off. Blocked.
strings.arena.rule.G2: The message claims the owner's policy or limits changed. Only the owner changes the policy, in the Policy Builder. Blocked.
strings.arena.rule.G3: The message names a different order than the link proves. Blocked.
strings.arena.rule.G19: The message names a different PayPal transaction than the one this link is for. That may be a typo, so it is held for the owner, not refused. Any refund goes only to the link's own transaction.
strings.arena.rule.G4: This order has already been refunded in full. Blocked.
strings.arena.rule.G5: This exact message was already sent for this order. Blocked.
strings.arena.rule.G6: The proposed amount is more than what is left to refund on this order. Blocked.
strings.arena.rule.G7: The proposed amount is above the owner's hard ceiling. Blocked.
strings.arena.rule.G8: The reader proposed no refund, so there is nothing to decide and nothing moves.
strings.arena.rule.G9: The message claims authority (owner, support, management). Words cannot grant authority. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G10: The message uses urgency or a threat. Pressure does not change the rule. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G11: The message asks for a repeat or for the rest of a refund. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G12: The message holds several different amounts, or the proposed amount does not match what it states. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G13: The reason is missing, or the owner does not allow it to be refunded automatically. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G14: The policy asks for the buyer's own words as evidence of the reason, and none were quoted. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G16: The buyer takes the request back, asks for something else instead, or makes the refund depend on a condition. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G17: The buyer's words are not a plain, unconditional request for money back that the desk can read with certainty: they ask something else, add a condition or a second thought, use wording outside the short list the desk accepts, or name an order or amount in a way the desk cannot verify. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.G15: Automatic refunds on this order would add up to more than the owner's allowance per order. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.R7: The amount is over the owner's limit for one automatic refund. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.R8: The amount would pass the owner's daily budget for automatic refunds. Held for the owner.
strings.arena.rule.R9: Inside the owner's policy. The refund goes out by itself (simulated here).

strings.arena.court.intro: A demo device. The buyer's words are the case. The rule evaluation is the verdict. The reader's argument cannot change it.

strings.arena.court.flag: The clerk notes a signal under rule {rule}: {category}. The buyer's words:
strings.arena.court.counterfactual: Without the attack signals the judge would have said {decision} under {rule}. The signals changed the verdict.
strings.arena.court.verdict_ESCALATE: ESCALATE under {rule} ({code}). {amount} is held for the owner. Nothing moved.
strings.policy.title: Policy Builder
strings.policy.intro: Write the refund rule in plain words. Code turns it into a fixed set of settings and checks it strictly. A model is not involved, and nothing you type is ever run as code. Words it does not know are rejected, not guessed.
strings.policy.box_hint: Settings you do not mention stay as they are.

strings.policy.field.eligible_reasons: Reasons that may be refunded automatically

strings.errors.RATE_LIMITED: Too many messages right now. Wait a little and try again.
strings.errors.UNKNOWN_ORDER: That order is not one of the sample orders.
strings.gate.G1: The message tries to give the helper new orders or to switch the rules off. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G2: The message claims the refund rule changed. Only you change the rule. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G3: The message names a different order than the buyer's link. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G19: The message names a different PayPal transaction than the buyer's link. That may be a typo, so it waits for you. If you approve, the refund goes to the link's own transaction, never to the one in the message.
strings.gate.G4: This order is already fully refunded. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G5: This exact message was already handled for this order. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G6: The amount, {amount}, is more than what is left to refund on this order. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G7: The amount, {amount}, is above your hard ceiling of {ceiling}. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G8: The helper found no refund to propose. Nothing was refunded.
strings.gate.G9: The message claims authority (owner, support or management). Words cannot grant that. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G10: The message uses urgency or a threat. Pressure does not change the rule. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G11: The message asks for a repeat or for the rest of an earlier refund. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G12: The message has several different amounts, or the proposed amount, {amount}, is not what the buyer wrote. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G13: The reason is missing, or it is not on your list of reasons that may be refunded without asking you. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G14: Your rule asks for the buyer's own words as evidence of the reason, and the quoted words did not support it. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G16: The buyer takes the request back, asks for something else instead, or makes the refund depend on a condition. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G18: This request was approved before it was sent, then the rule, the limits or the records changed before it went out. It was closed without sending and the buyer can write again.
strings.gate.G17: The buyer's words are not a plain, unconditional request the desk can read with certainty (wording outside its short list, an added condition, or an order or amount it cannot verify), so this proposal waits for you.
strings.gate.G17.UNREAD_NO_MODEL: The desk could not read part of this message with certainty (a sentence outside the wording it knows), and no AI reading was available to settle it, so it waits for you.
strings.gate.G17.MODEL_UNAVAILABLE: An AI reading of this message is switched on, but it could not be had (a timeout, a refusal or a reply the desk does not accept), so nothing goes out by itself. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G17.MODEL_DECLINED: The AI reading did not call this a single plain request for money back, so it waits for you. The flags and its one-line reason are below.
strings.gate.G17.MODEL_QUOTE_INVALID: The AI reading said this was a plain request, but the words it pointed to are not the buyer's own request, so it waits for you.
strings.gate.G17.MODEL_READING_INVALID: The AI reading came back in a shape the desk does not accept, so it waits for you.
strings.gate.G17.RULES_HAZARD: The desk's fixed rules found something in the buyer's words that holds a refund for a person (a condition, a withdrawal, another payee, wording aimed at the system, or an unclear amount). An AI reading cannot override that. It waits for you.
strings.gate.G17.BINDING_SEVERAL_ORDERS: The message names more than one order, so it waits for you.
strings.gate.G17.BINDING_PARSE_MISMATCH_AMOUNT: The dollar amounts read two different ways from the same words (something hides a figure), so it waits for you.

strings.hold.untrusted_note: The quoted words and the AI's sentence are untrusted text.

strings.desk.title: Refund Desk
strings.desk.intro: Even when the reader is compromised, automatic refunds remain within merchant-set limits. Larger requests, and requests that match a recognized suspicious pattern, wait for the owner; some patterns are refused outright. The limits bound what a wrong or hostile proposal can cost. They do not tell you whether a buyer is honest.
strings.desk.mode_fake: SIMULATION: PayPal answers come from a synthetic fixture. Reader in use for typed messages: {reader}.
strings.desk.mode_sandbox: Connected to your own PayPal sandbox app. Reader in use for typed messages: {reader}.
strings.desk.group.legit: Ordinary requests (read by the model if one is set up, otherwise by a scripted test model)
strings.desk.group.hostile: Hostile messages (read by the configured reader)
strings.desk.group.compromised_note: The reader is replaced by a scripted one that proposes whatever the attacker wants, with convincing evidence. These go straight to the same authority.
strings.desk.flow_empty: No request yet. Pick a sample request or write your own. The verdict appears here, with what the AI suggested and what your rule decided.
strings.desk.score_title: How we count: four measures, kept apart
strings.desk.score_caveat: These figures describe this library and this log only. They are not a claim about all attacks, and they say nothing about whether a buyer is telling the truth.
strings.desk.buyer_line: Request {id}, order {order}. The order comes from the buyer's link, never from the words.
strings.desk.reader_none: No proposal was made. The buyer was asked for more information.
strings.desk.reader_untrusted: Everything the reader says is a suggestion. The authority checks it against the buyer's own words and your numbers.
strings.desk.exchange: Model reply: {verdict}. Instructions and buyer text sent separately: {sep}.
strings.desk.reader.scripted: scripted test model (canned reply through the real validator, not a live model)
strings.desk.route.AUTO: Inside your rule: it goes out by itself and counts toward your daily automatic budget.
strings.desk.route.REVIEW: Held for you. A refund you approve by hand is outside the daily automatic budget, and it still has to fit what is left on the order.
strings.desk.route.BLOCKED: Refused. Nothing was sent to PayPal.
strings.desk.owner_bound: Your yes is bound to exactly this: {amount} for order {order}, under the rule version shown. If the rule changes before you answer, the yes is refused.
strings.desk.owner_denied: You declined. Nothing was sent to PayPal.
strings.desk.owner_not_needed: No approval needed. It was inside your rule.
strings.desk.owner_blocked: No approval offered. A hard rule refused it.
strings.desk.owner_none: Nothing for you to decide here.
strings.desk.no_refund: No refund exists for this request. Nothing was sent to PayPal.
strings.desk.readback.fixture: Read from the synthetic fixture, not from PayPal.
strings.desk.readback.sandbox: Read from PayPal's refund resource in your sandbox.
strings.desk.readback_failed: Could not read the refund back ({reason}). Nothing is assumed.
strings.desk.readback_ok: The refund resource matches what we sent.
strings.desk.readback_bad: The refund resource does not match. Look into it.
strings.desk.capture_ok: Refunds PayPal confirms for this order: {confirmed} of {captured} captured.
strings.desk.capture_bad: Could not confirm the order's refunds against the captured amount ({confirmed} of {captured}).
strings.desk.score.calls_line: {n} sent, {refunds} refunds with a provider id.
strings.desk.score.calls_note: Counted from signed receipts. A refused, held or denied request adds nothing here.
strings.desk.score.limits_line: {n} automatic refunds checked against your numbers. {v} broke one.
strings.desk.score.limits_note: Audited from the signed receipts, apart from the gate. Says nothing about honesty.
strings.desk.score.auth_line: {n} automatic refunds checked. {u} had no signed ALLOW behind them.
strings.desk.score.auth_note: Every automatic refund must trace to a signed decision.
strings.desk.score.attack_line: {n} labeled attacks. {x} got money automatically, {b} refused outright, {o} sent to you.
strings.desk.score.attack_reader: The reader went along with {w} of {n}.
strings.desk.score.attack_note: A pure attack is owed nothing, so any automatic release counts here, even inside every limit.
strings.desk.score.legit_line: {n} labeled ordinary requests. {a} completed by themselves, {o} waiting for you, {p} approved by you, {r} refused, {u} unresolved (PayPal did not answer).
strings.desk.score.legit_note: Availability, kept apart from safety. Refusing everything would score perfectly on 1 to 3 and badly here.
strings.desk.score.other_line: {n} typed messages. {x} released automatically, {o} sent to you, {b} refused. Only measures 1 and 2 apply to them.
strings.arena.budget_used: Automatic refunds so far today (simulated): {used} of {daily}.
strings.arena.budget_note: These limits do not move. One visitor cannot lower them for the next.
strings.desk.owner_approved: You approved it. Your yes was bound to this amount, this order and this version of the rule.
strings.desk.owner_expired: Nobody answered in time. It closed and nothing was sent to PayPal.
strings.desk.fault_note: The refund request goes out, then PayPal's answer is lost. The fault is switched on for the next request only, and it exists only in the simulation.
strings.desk.unknown_title: Unresolved: we do not know whether PayPal made this refund
strings.desk.unknown_body: The refund request was sent and no usable answer came back. The money stays held, the buyer is told it is being checked, and this screen sends no second request, and a new message for this order is held back until this is settled.
strings.desk.unknown_held: {amount} is held on order {order}. Dispatch attempts recorded before sending, so far: {sent}.
strings.desk.recheck.FOUND: PayPal's own record of the refund was read. It is now recorded as sent and was read back.
strings.desk.recheck.NO_KNOWN_ID: No refund id is in our records, so this re-check made no request to PayPal and read nothing from it. It does not show whether PayPal made the refund, and this build cannot search PayPal by request key. The outcome stays unknown and the money stays held. Look for a refund on this payment in your PayPal dashboard before you do anything else. No refund request was sent.
strings.desk.recheck.UNREADABLE: We hold a refund id but PayPal could not be read (or its answer did not match), or the lookup window has passed. It is still unresolved. No refund request was sent.
strings.desk.recheck.NOT_UNRESOLVED: There is nothing left to check. Nothing was sent.
strings.desk.unknown_repeat_blocked: Another message for this order is held back while this is unresolved.
strings.policy.err.PER_REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED: A limit per single refund is not something this build enforces. The allowance is per order and adds up across refunds. Say "per order" instead.
strings.policy.err.PREVIEW_REQUIRED: A rule can only be saved after it was checked: the check gives the version and result that the save must carry. Nothing was saved. Check the rule first.
strings.policy.err.POLICY_CHANGED: The rule in force changed after you checked yours. Nothing was saved. Check the rule again.
strings.policy.err.PREVIEW_MISMATCH: The text no longer gives the result you were shown. Nothing was saved. Check the rule again.
strings.policy.enforced_note: These are the numbers the refund engine itself holds, read back from the engine and not from this page's own copy.
strings.policy.enforced_ceiling: Most you can approve in one refund: {value}
strings.policy.enforced_match: Matches the policy in force: yes
strings.policy.enforced_mismatch: Matches the policy in force: NO. Do not rely on this screen.
strings.policy.save_binds: Saving applies exactly the result shown here, to version {version}. If the rule in force changes first, the save is refused.
strings.policy.example_hint: Click a phrase to add it to your rule.
strings.policy.saved_note: Approval cards shown under the old version can no longer be approved. Deny them; the buyer writes again.
strings.desk.enforced_line: Enforced by the engine now (version {version}): allowance {cap} per order, {daily} per day, approve up to {ceiling} per refund.
strings.desk.owner_stale: You saved a new rule after this card was made, so a yes can no longer be given to it. Deny it; the buyer writes again and the new rule decides.
strings.desk.owner_policy_version: This yes applies to rule version {version} only.
strings.stamp.reason.unknown: The refund request was sent and PayPal's answer did not come back.
strings.stamp.reason.failed: PayPal received the request and did not complete the refund.
strings.stamp.reason.not_sent: The request could not be sent.
strings.stamp.out.sent_sim: {amount} refund sent to the simulated PayPal. No real money moved.
strings.stamp.out.sent_sandbox: {amount} refund sent to your PayPal sandbox. Sandbox money only.
strings.stamp.out.sent_pending_sim: {amount} refund sent to the simulated PayPal. It is not marked complete yet.
strings.stamp.out.sent_pending_sandbox: {amount} refund sent to your PayPal sandbox. PayPal has not marked it complete yet.
strings.stamp.out.nothing: $0.00 left the shop. Nothing was sent to PayPal.
strings.stamp.out.held: Nothing was sent. {amount} waits for your OK.
strings.stamp.out.held_stale: Nothing was sent. Your rule changed after this was held, so you can only deny it.
strings.stamp.out.unknown: {amount} stays held. We do not know whether PayPal made this refund.
strings.stamp.out.failed: PayPal did not complete the refund. Look into it.
strings.stamp.out.ask: No clear amount or reason. Nothing was sent.
strings.stamp.out.pending_check: It will be checked automatically. Nothing was sent.
strings.stamp.out.mismatch: Nothing can be done with this request. Look into it.
strings.stamp.arena.sent: {amount} released to the simulated PayPal. No real money moved.
strings.stamp.arena.held: Nothing moved. No owner is online in the arena, so this request closes.
strings.stamp.compare: The AI suggested {suggested}. Your rule let {allowed} through.
strings.stamp.compare_held: The AI suggested {suggested}. Your rule let $0.00 through so far.
strings.stamp.compare_unknown: The AI suggested {suggested}. Whether any of it went out is not known yet.
strings.panel.suggest_tag: Model suggestion. Not trusted, not checked.
strings.panel.decide_tag: Code decision. Your numbers, not the AI's.
strings.chip.label: Where this screen's data comes from
strings.footer.notice: Not affiliated with or endorsed by PayPal. PayPal is named only as the platform this entry runs on. Simulated or sandbox data only; no real money moves.
strings.desk.lede: A buyer writes. The AI suggests a refund. Your rule decides what goes out.
strings.desk.about_title: What this desk claims, and what it does not
strings.tile.fooled_sub: labelled attack messages this session. Not an evaluation.
strings.tile.breach_sub: automatic refunds, checked against your numbers by a separate check.
strings.tile.held_label: Ordinary sample requests held for you
strings.tile.attack_note: {x} of {n} labelled attacks got an automatic refund this session. An attack inside your allowance can still be paid: the limits cap what a lie costs, they do not detect it.
strings.approve.title: Approve a refund?
strings.approve.binding: This yes is for {amount} on order {order}, under rule version {version}. If the rule changes first, it can only be denied.
strings.approve.nothing: There is nothing to approve here.
strings.approve.missing: This approval card was not found.
strings.arena.details: Show the details: difference, signals, rule trace and receipt
